Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)
- Primary assessment: Acute unilateral left-sided headache with visual disturbances (blurry vision and zigzag lines), dizziness, and nausea/vomiting beginning this morning; pain peak ~6/10; no focal neurological deficits reported; patient able to ambulate with preference to rest; first-time presentation for this type of headache
- Likely diagnosis (consistent with transcript): Migraine with aura
  - Rationale: Unilateral left-headache with visual aura (zigzag lines, blurred vision), nausea/vomiting, photophobia, worsened by movement; family history of migraines supporting susceptibility
- Differential diagnoses considered (supported by DDx, aligned with transcript):
  - Subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH) / acute intracranial vascular event — Moderate
    - Rationale: Sudden onset headache with vomiting; red flags warrant full neurological assessment if symptoms persist or worsen
  - Ischemic stroke / transient ischemic attack (TIA) with visual symptoms — Moderate
    - Rationale: Acute onset headache with visual disturbance and dizziness; absence of motor deficits does not exclude vascular events
- Contradictions or uncertainties: No explicit contradictions between transcript and DDx; migraine remains the leading diagnosis based on presentation
- DDx alignment: See Summary of Differential Diagnoses

Management Plan
- Medications discussed:
  - Paracetamol (taken by patient prior to visit) — dose/route/frequency not documented
  - Ibuprofen (recommended as migraine treatment) — dose/route/frequency not documented
  - Antiemetic (not specified) — dose/route/frequency not documented
- Nonpharmacologic/adjunct measures:
  - Avoid screens; rest in a quiet, darkened environment
  - Ingest sugary/carbonated beverage (e.g., cola) as part of supportive therapy
- Observations and monitoring:
  - If symptoms improve with initial treatment, continue management and arrange same-day neurological assessment today
  - If symptoms worsen or fail to improve, seek urgent in-person evaluation (emergency/ED) for a full neurological exam and potential investigations
- Investigations:
  - Not performed in this encounter; no labs or imaging ordered
- Referrals/Follow-up:
  - Plan for same-day neurological assessment
  - If improvement occurs, cancellation of appointment is acceptable with prior notification
- Other considerations:
  - Consider potential red flags requiring urgent care if new deficits develop (weakness, numbness, speech difficulties, severe neck stiffness, fever, altered mental status)

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)
- Migraine with aura — High
  - Justification: Unilateral left headache with visual aura, nausea/vomiting, photophobia, and improvement with migraine-directed measures; positive family history of migraine supports likelihood
- Subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH) — Moderate
  - Justification: Sudden onset headache with vomiting; red flags warrant evaluation to exclude a vascular catastrophe
- Ischemic stroke / TIA with visual symptoms — Moderate
  - Justification: Acute onset with visual disturbance and dizziness; absence of motor deficits reduces likelihood but vascular etiologies remain a consideration
